topic.title: Sara Blakely Started Spanx With Her Fax Machine Savings

title: She Started Spanx With $5,000
description:
What did Sara Blakely's fax machine savings turn into?
Spanx, from one pair of cut-up pantyhose in 2000 to the Blackstone deal in 2021, told from the reporting.
Sources: CNN Business (Oct 2021).
Based on public records and reporting. Not financial or legal advice.

lines.text: Sara Blakely started Spanx with $5,000 she had saved selling fax machines.
Her whole idea was one pair of pantyhose, with the feet cut off.
She called it Spanx in 2000, in Atlanta, and wrote the patent application herself.
Her first big order came from Neiman Marcus. But how far could one product go?
For years she owned all of it, with no investors. So what was it really worth?
Then in October, the investment firm Blackstone bought most of it.
That deal valued Spanx, the company that started with one pair of pantyhose, at $1.2B.
She kept a big piece too. Scissors or the sales job: which one built Spanx? Remember,

Facts confirmed on the source page (CNN Business via ABC17, 21 Oct 2021): $5,000 savings, founded 2000, valued at $1.2B with Blackstone taking a majority stake, Blakely keeping a significant stake. The verify item holds: the script says 'bought most of it' and 'valued', not a price paid. Narrative claims confirmed by search (Fortune 2025, Stanford GSB 2018, Entrepreneur, Wikipedia): the savings came from selling fax machines, Atlanta, she wrote the patent herself, Neiman Marcus was the first major order, self-funded with no outside investors until 2021. No advice, tone is right, disclaimer is in the description. Note: the voice says 'in October' with no year; the on-screen date shows 2021.
